questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important to choose a study destination where English is the main language spoken.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I think the information needed was fairly easy to find. But to be fair I do have an uncle living in Sydney that could answer any additional questions I had (mostly about Covid though).

UOW have a good and easy webside and if you need any additional information just pop them an email and you will get an answer quickly. 
The visa process was a bit long but the information was not hard to get.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the student central for help with finalising my subject schedule.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I though the O-week would have information and introduction to various aspects of the uni life here but we had one day with information and the rest of the week was just going out drinking. Furthermore was the information already available online and the introduction to the clubs was the week after.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: At my accommodation you could live in a shared apartment 4 people or in a studio. (Kooloobong)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
At my 4 share we had a pretty big kitchen with oven. (In the building 73, 74 and 75 they don't have ovens in the apartment).
There is also a common kitchen in every building and an outdoor barbecue.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
the kitchens in the apartments are empty. This means you have to buy your own crockery, cutlery, kettle, pots and pans. 
The only thing available in the kitchen upon arrival is a microwave.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In my building there was construction going on during the whole term, which I was not made aware of before I got here. This meant no acces to my balcony and a lot of noice between 7-17. The people who worked there was very helpfull though and I am told i will receive compensation. 
The apartments are nice enough (beside the kitchen being empty). I did meet all of my friends at my accommodation and they host social event weekly.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out a form on their webside. I don't remember the process being complicated at all. I enrolled in more subjects than possible and got them all pre-approved at KU and UOW and then dropped the least exiting classes in the drop-period in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was available via email from UOW and the study abroad office at KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
100% succesfull in the classes i applied for. 
The only thing is that some of the classes I found interesting was only available in the fall semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
be aware that the Australian spring and fall are opposite the Danish when you look into classes.
Choose an Indigenous class if you are given the option!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: they still had online lectures in most of my classes. In some of them it wasn't really optimal but I did really like the possibility to see them multiple times and on my own schedule.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one 100 level class, one 200 level class and two 300 level classes and I'm on my 5th semester in my bachelor degree

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Most of my classes had a "flipped classroom" style. This meant that the lectures were online and prerecorded. I was expected to do watch the lecture and do all the reading and sometimes answer questions before my tutorials.  
The tutorials were much more discussion based than at KU. 
There is required attendance so you can't skip classes (unless you are sick ofc). 
The presentations, quizzes and essays you do doing the semester counts as a percentage of your final grade. therefore the actual exam is only 30-50%.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON318 (Spring)  Economics of Health and Human Resources
INDS130 (Spring)  Indigenous Knowledge in Global Contexts
POL 309 (Spring)  Global Political Economy
STS 216 (Spring)  Environmental Sustainability, Risk and Governance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Global Political Economy (POL309). I really enjoyed the combination of politcal science and economics. The subject also gave a good historical view on the political ideologies. The exam is a "book chapter" on a self chosen subject, which makes it really interesting.
I would also recommend to do an Indigenous class if possible. It gives a great perspective on some of the the past and present challenges in Australia and a non-eurocentric view on colonisation.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: busses are free in Wollongong so I did not expect to spend money on transport, but i went to Sydney a few weekends which ofc costs some money. Alcohol is pretty expensive too and groceries are somewhat the same as in DK i think but hard to know with inflation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was s expected. I spend less on food than I though i would but that is mainly cause i cooked a lot at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In week 2 there is hosted clubs day where all the clubs presenting themselves at the duck pond lawn. The uni club also host some free activities every week and Kooloobong also have activities and clubs you can join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I tried the volleyball club which was great and with some lovely people! I also went to free yoga every Tuesday morning and free breakfast every Wednesday morning hosted by uni club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around Australia if you have the possibility!
I rented a car with some friends and drove up to Brisbane in my springbreak, which i would highly recommend. 
After exams we did a roadtrip from Melbourne to Adelaide and then I travelled to Darwin and Cairns afterwards. Australia is also a great place to do some solo travelling and you meet some many nice people at hostels.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Australians are really open and welcoming. They are also very interested in people from other countries.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some clubs at uni!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The part days in NSW is Wednesday and Sunday. This was a really bad fit with my school schedule and it felt pretty weird to me to go out on weekdays.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hanging out in nature part was great! To meet up with friends and family in the botanical garden and use the free barbecues is great. Or meeting up with friends on the beach every time the weather is good to hang out, surf and play some volley. The culture is pretty laid back vibe which i enjoyed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take advantage of the great lokation of Wollongong! your weekends can be filled with:
1. Hikes in the Royal National Park
2. City get away to Sydney
3. Beach days in one of the beaches in Wollongong

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's pretty easy to rent a car for a day or a week and it is so much easier to get around when you have a car. Australia is defiantly made primarily for cars!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people are met there, the nature I saw and trying the study style they have in a different country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit annoying that the summer/ winter is flipped so that classes started so early. This meant that I did not really have a summer break between my exams at KU and the semester start at UOW. Therefore all my travels had to wait for after exams at UOW and at that point I did miss people at home a bit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Wollongong has a great location and campus is really pretty!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
